docs.title: Semantic Workspace
docs.text:
The Semantic Workspace maps unstructured sources onto a semantic layer that is given and never edited. The sources are documents, fill-in forms and recorded calls. The results are evidence links and an anchored concept catalog. The workspace can also write table rows as a system feature, which the paper does not cover. A question-answering workspace reads those results and cites the passages behind each answer.

This site describes the design and the details. It is written from the working paper and from the code. It holds no lab exercises.

Figure 1 of the paper. (a) At build time, Pipeline A links passages to the given semantic model (Output A). Pipeline B groups that evidence into concepts (Output B). A person approves and publishes a release. (b) At question time, a rules-first router sends each request to one of four fixed tools; a model helps only with a request to act that the rules do not complete.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
Structured data has a semantic layer. The layer names each field and metric, defines it and declares how tables join. Contracts, forms and recorded calls have no such layer. The limits, dates and commitments they hold cannot be joined to the tables or governed with them.

The paper frames this gap as a mapping task. For each passage, decide which definitions it states a value of or is about, or abstain. Then group that evidence into business concepts linked to the layer. The layer is the target. The system never edits it.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
One rule runs through the design: the model chooses, code decides.

  • A small language model picks among retrieved definitions.
  • Deterministic guards check the stated value, settle the relation and attach entity keys.
  • Concepts of the layer collect their evidence by aggregation, with no model call.
  • Only passages the layer cannot explain reach an induction model.
  • At question time, code computes every number. The model writes a plan and reads clause values.

docs.title: Headline results and limits
docs.text:
The paper reports these results. The scope of each is part of the claim.

Result Value Scope Link precision, model decision step 0.70 Held-out gold set A2, run once, 82 anchors Link precision, thresholds and rules 0.29 Same set Precision on unseen packs, two-step 0.73 (finance), 0.90 (manufacturing) Generator-made synthetic packs, run once False-link rate on unseen packs, two-step 0.03 (finance), 0.01 (manufacturing) Same packs Question answering, unseen exams 11, 14, 18 and 17 of 30 Four exams; none meets the pass bar

Limits stated by the paper

Recall on commitments is the main limit. The evaluation sets are small, and one AI annotator wrote each set. The sets cover two demo datasets. The question-answering path does not meet its pass bar on any unseen exam. The paper does not claim state-of-the-art results.

See Evaluation for every table and its scope.

docs.title: Reading guide
docs.text:
Read in this order for the design.

  1. Concepts: the task, the terms and a glossary.
  2. Architecture: build time, question time, components and data stores.
  3. Ingestion: how each file type becomes passages.
  4. Pipeline A: passages to evidence links.
  5. Pipeline B: evidence links to a concept catalog.
  6. Review and release: human decisions and what reaches answers.

Read these for use and operation.

  • Ask: the question path, the router, refusals and citations.
  • Table rows: table rows from forms, printed reports, calls and documents, and the two write paths.
  • Access and masking: accounts, withheld sources and identifier masking.
  • Localization: the English and Chinese language switch.
  • Deployment: the AMP on Cloudera AI.
  • Data: the two sample datasets and their licences.

docs.title: The paper
docs.text: Mapping Unstructured Documents onto a Governed Semantic Layer: Evidence Links and an Anchored Concept Catalog. Working draft, 23 November 2026, not reviewed. The PDF is in the repository at docs/paper/main.pdf.

docs.title: Two datasets
docs.text:
The workspace ships with two demo datasets.

Dataset Structured data Unstructured sources Financial Services A mock-up banking workbook, 11 tables, three days of transactions Synthetic banking documents, fill-in forms, one recorded call Manufacturing AdventureWorks sample data, 25 tables Synthetic contracts and AdventureWorks sample documents

The finance model has 143 definitions. The manufacturing model has 240 definitions. See Data for what is synthetic, what is public and the attribution.

docs.title: Terms used on this site
docs.text:
• Cloudera AI hosts the application and its jobs as an AMP.
  • Cloudera Lakehouse Engine (Trino) is the direct write path for table rows to Iceberg.
  • Semantic Hub is the target of the release export. A release is an Ossie file that passes the Semantic Hub schema check and lint.

docs.title: Access and masking
docs.text: Access is checked on every request. A withheld source is never read, cited or summarised for the principal it is withheld from. Restricted identifiers are masked in every JSON reply, at the response boundary.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
The workspace ships five demonstration accounts. They live in the private PostgreSQL.

Account Role Datasets admin admin Financial Services, Manufacturing finance_reader reader Financial Services finance_restricted restricted Financial Services manufacturing_reader reader Manufacturing manufacturing_restricted restricted Manufacturing

Roles grant capabilities.

Role Capabilities admin query, view insights, upload, process, review, publish, build the graph, build the catalog reader query, view insights restricted query, view insights; some sources withheld

docs.title: Withheld sources
docs.text:
Each restricted account has sources withheld.

  • Financial Services restricted reader: an adverse-media report and the recorded call.
  • Manufacturing restricted reader: two contracts.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
A session is a random token in a cookie. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash. A session lasts eight hours. The first visit opens an admin session. Switching account replaces the session.

Demonstration accounts

These accounts are for demonstration. They have no passwords. Use them only on a deployment that is itself access-controlled, such as a Cloudera AI application.

docs.title: Where access is enforced
docs.text: Place Rule Every /api/* route The dataset must be granted to the principal Chunks and links A chunk from a withheld source is not visible Concepts A concept with any withheld evidence passage hides its examples and empties its synonyms for that reader Document-only concepts The meaning is replaced by a withheld notice Answers A concept with any withheld passage is left out; a question only a withheld source can answer is refused as "source withheld" Releases A release with content from a source the account cannot read is hidden Fact detail Withheld sources are refused with the compiler's own check Progress trace Names no source beyond what the reply itself says Entity 360 Every link, passage and concept passes the visibility check

docs.title: Why concepts need care
docs.text: A concept's label, meaning and synonyms are written by a model from all of its evidence. A withheld passage could leak through them. The paper reports such a fault, found late. The catalog route returned a concept's examples, phrases copied from evidence chunks. One came from a withheld source. The fix hides examples, empties synonyms and replaces document-only meanings when any evidence passage is withheld. A meaning anchored on the model stays, because it comes from the model.

docs.title: Identifier masking
docs.text:
The data model says of some columns: never display the value. The server masks those values in every JSON reply.

Kind Columns matched by name Account AccountNumber, AccountNo, AccNum, CounterpartyAccountNo Customer CustomerID Relationship manager RMID

docs.title: What is masked
docs.text:
The set of values to mask has two parts.

  • Values the restricted columns hold. These are read once.
  • Values that evidence links state for a restricted column, such as an identifier said on a call that no table holds. These are re-read every 20 seconds. A stated value needs a letter or eight digits, because a short bare number may be a misread amount.

Values of four characters or fewer are not collected.

docs.title: How it is masked
docs.text:
Every string in a reply is scanned for whole tokens that hold a digit. A token equal to a restricted value is replaced. A digit-only token that is part of a decimal or grouped number is left alone. An integer field whose name is a restricted column is masked too.

The masked form keeps the tail:

•••• 1234     (values of eight characters or more keep four)
•••• 34       (shorter values keep two)

Token matching uses ASCII classes only. An identifier written next to Chinese text with no space still stands as a token.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
• Source identities (id, sourceId, hashes) are left intact.
  • The Entity 360 route keeps customer and relationship-manager identifiers, because it is searched by them. Account numbers stay masked there.

docs.title: Identity numbers
docs.text: National identity numbers in extracted text are masked before the text reaches the browser. The pattern comes from the inherited field extractor in multimedia_rag/fields.py. Stored form cells hold the masked value.

docs.title: Entities are never merged
docs.text: Entities keep the key they are known by. A name in a document never resolves to a customer identifier. A customer identifier stated in a call transcript may differ by one character from an identifier in the table. The two are shown as similar and are never merged.

docs.title: Request origin
docs.text:
The server accepts same-origin requests only.

  • The Host header must be the loopback address with the server port, or a host named in V2_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
  • A cross-site or same-site fetch is refused.
  • A request with an Origin header must come from the same host.
  • A request that changes state must carry an Origin header.

Behind the Cloudera AI application proxy, set V2_ALLOWED_HOSTS to the application's public host name. See Deployment.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The system has two phases. At build time it turns sources into evidence links, a concept catalog and a published release. At question time a small harness routes each request to one fixed tool. Both phases run in one Python server process with a private PostgreSQL and a local vector index.

Figure 1 of the paper. The right panel shows one demo question answered from a letter and its amendment. A refusal replaces the three result parts when no answer is supported.

docs.title: Build time
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  S[Sources<br/>documents, forms, calls] --> P[Passages<br/>split, pinned by hash]
  G[Given<br/>tables and semantic model] --> A
  P --> A[Pipeline A<br/>score, shortlist, decide, guard, resolve]
  A --> OA[(Output A<br/>evidence links)]
  OA --> B[Pipeline B<br/>anchor, induce, merge, vote]
  G --> B
  B --> OB[(Output B<br/>concept catalog)]
  OB --> H{{Person<br/>approve, correct, reject}}
  H --> R[(Release<br/>Ossie export)]
  P --> T[Template links<br/>form fields]
  T --> OC[(Table rows<br/>after a confirm)]
  1. Ingestion turns each source into passages. See Ingestion.
  2. Pipeline A writes evidence links for each passage. See Pipeline A.
  3. Pipeline B reads all links and writes the concept catalog. See Pipeline B.
  4. A person reviews the links and concepts and publishes a release. See Review and release.
  5. For declared form templates, code fills table rows. See Table rows.

Four of the eleven algorithm steps call a language model. Code does the rest.

docs.title: Question time
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Q[Ask text] --> RT{Router<br/>code rules}
  RT -->|write wording| W[Write a table<br/>preview, then confirm]
  RT -->|what does X mean| E[Explain a term<br/>concept, definition, passages]
  RT -->|connections, targets| C[Connections<br/>write targets]
  RT -->|otherwise| AN[Answer path]
  AN --> G1[Gate] --> O[Offer] --> PL[Plan<br/>model call 1] --> BI[Bind] --> F[Facts<br/>guarded SQL]
  F --> RD[Read<br/>model call 2] --> D[Decide<br/>code]
  D --> REP[Reply: status, facts,<br/>citations, conclusion]

The router is code first; a model helps only with a request to act that the rules do not complete, and code checks its reply. It names a tool. It never writes. The answer path makes one or two model calls. Code computes every number and selects the citations. See Ask.

docs.text:
All state lives under one state directory outside the repository.

docs.title: Write rules
docs.text:
• No write reaches a shared table without a preview and a human confirm.
  • A confirm needs the preview's fingerprint and a one-use approval.
  • Writes from Ask are limited to the administrator.
  • Answer results go to insert-only tables, so a replay adds nothing.

docs.title: Ask
docs.text: Ask is a small harness around the answer path. Code rules route each text to one of four fixed tools. A model helps only when a request to act is worded in a way the rules do not complete. The answer path joins SQL facts with cited document clauses. It makes one or two model calls. Code computes every number and decides the status, the arithmetic and the citations.

docs.title: The router
docs.text:
The router is code first. It names a tool and its arguments. It never runs one. It checks the rules in this order.

Order Tool Rule 1 Write a table The text asks to write, save or load, and names a table or the lakehouse. A question is never a write. 2 Explain a term The text asks what a term means: "what does X mean", "define X", "meaning of X". 3 Connections The text names a connection or a write target. 4 Answer Otherwise: a question about the data and documents.

A polite request such as "can you write this to Iceberg?" counts as a request, not a question. A write tool only produces a preview. The write itself needs a separate confirm. See Table rows.

docs.title: When the rules are not enough
docs.text:
Some requests to act are worded in a way the rules do not complete, such as "Add report 3 and report 4 to the transactions". For such a text, and only for it, the router makes one model call. A plain question never causes this call.

  • The model receives the fixed tool list, the files this account may read and the declared tables. It replies with one tool and its arguments as JSON.
  • Code checks every argument. The tool must be in the list. Each file must be readable. A table must resolve to exactly one declared table.
  • The text itself must name each file and the table. If the model picks one the text does not name, the app asks back.
  • An unusable reply falls back to the rules. An unclear request gets a clarification that lists the real choices.
  • The trace shows how the route was chosen: by the rules, by the model, or by the rules after an unusable model reply.

A write chosen this way is still only a preview.

docs.title: Clarifications offer choices
docs.text:
When a request is ambiguous, the app asks back. It does not guess. If the clarification is a choice among things the semantic layer already knows, the card offers them as buttons.

  • Several definitions, concepts, records with the same name, or files match: each is a button with its label and a one-line meaning.
  • One definition needs a value from a short set, such as a business date, a currency or a year: the values are buttons.
  • The value comes from a large set, such as hundreds of products: the card gives a plain sentence with a few examples.
  • The semantic layer offers no real choice: the card shows only the question.

Code builds the choices from the published concepts, the model definitions and the data. No model is called. A click sends a complete request as the next turn. The person can always type instead. A choice never shows a value the account may not read, and an account without the write right is refused at once.

The published concepts (Output B) are used when a release exists. Without a release, the choices come from the given semantic model only.

docs.title: Chat sessions
docs.text:
A chat session lasts until the user starts a new one. The browser keeps the sessions; the server keeps none. Each later request carries the last turns as short quoted data. When a text may lean on earlier turns, one model call rewrites it into a standalone request, for example "and for 2022?". Code checks that the rewrite keeps every identifier and number of the new text. If the check fails, the text is read as typed. The answer shows the rewritten request as "Understood as". Opening a past session shows the stored turns. It sends no request and repeats no write.

The explain tool shows the concept, the definition and the passages from Output B. The connections tool lists write targets. Secrets stay on the server.

docs.title: The answer path
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  G[1 Gate<br/>code] --> O[2 Offer<br/>code]
  O --> P[3 Plan<br/>model call 1]
  P -->|invalid| RP[One named repair] --> P2{Valid?}
  P2 -->|no| REF[Refusal]
  P2 -->|yes| B
  P --> B[4 Bind<br/>code]
  B --> F[5 Facts<br/>guarded SQL]
  F --> R[6 Read<br/>model call 2, skipped when no document evidence is needed]
  R --> D[7 Decide<br/>code]
  B -->|missing or ambiguous parameter| CL[Clarification]
  B -->|party no record identifies| REF

Input: a question, the asking principal, the semantic model, the structured data, the readable chunks, Output A, and the approved concepts of the latest release of Output B. Output: the answer.

  1. Gate (code). The dataset and the model source must be readable by the principal.
  2. Offer (code). Code lists what the question states and the data can resolve: entities, periods and plain numbers. Entities are exact identifiers, names that equal a span of the question in a name column, and keys a referenced document states. Periods are parsed, never guessed. An approved concept's label or synonym is offered when the question states it.
  3. Plan (model call 1). A model writes a typed JSON plan: the measure, its aggregate, entities, value filters, time, the answer kind, the document evidence needed, a comparison, and what no definition supports. Every id must come from the definitions or the offered items. An invalid plan gets one repair that names the broken item. A second invalid plan is a refusal.
  4. Bind (code). Stated values are linked against the distinct values of their column. Entities are placed through declared relationships. A missing required parameter is a clarification that names it. An ambiguous value is a clarification. A party no record identifies is a refusal.
  5. Facts (code). A guarded SQL compiler computes the facts. Joins follow declared many-to-one relationships of up to three hops. A distinct count crosses a bridge table from the base table. No model supplies a number.
  6. Read (model call 2). Code ranks clauses from readable sources. A model names a clause for each evidence need and copies its value. Code checks that the copy is verbatim, parses it, and checks that the clause's document is tied to the named party.
  7. Decide (code). Code sets the status, does any comparison or arithmetic, writes the conclusion and selects at most four citations. The model writes the summary only.

A failed model call is a refusal, never a made-up answer. A question costs one or two model calls, plus at most one repair each. The default model is mistral-small-latest. V2_ANSWER_MODEL selects another.

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
Status Meaning answered Facts, a conclusion and citations clarify A missing parameter or an ambiguous value; the reply names it refused No supported answer, or the source is withheld; the reply gives the reason

A refusal replaces the result parts when no answer is supported.

docs.title: The reply
docs.text:
• Status, reason and refusal reason.
  • Definitions used.
  • Facts with value, SQL and filters.
  • At most four citations.
  • The conclusion and any comparison, computed by code.
  • A summary written by the model.
  • The plan.
  • The catalog concepts the question named and whether the plan used them.
  • A server-held handle per fact.

The reply is returned to the caller. It is not stored.

docs.title: Guards added in rounds 3 to 7
docs.text:
Each guard is a mechanism in code, not a word list for one question. This table shows a selection.

Mechanism What it prevents One period parser (day, range, month, month end, quarter, half year, year) Guessed dates; a period read in different ways by different steps Named repair of an invalid plan An accidental refusal from one malformed plan item A record a cited clause names narrows the measure; never another party's record An answer about a different account, deal or order Declared joins of up to three hops; a bridge table for a distinct count Refusal of two-hop questions; double counting through a join Commitment rule: agreeing, committing, promising or certifying sends the question to documents A recorded figure presented as what a party agreed Withheld-source rule: when only a withheld source holds the answer, refuse as "source withheld" An answer built from the readable remainder Direction-word rule: "credit" or "debit" binds the one column value it names, or asks A total that mixes debits and credits Period outside the data: refuse before checking for a missing parameter A request for a parameter when no parameter can help Reference-token rule: a report, contract or order number no table key holds must be stated by every cited source A figure from a different report Catalog-name narrowing rules A reviewed name overriding the model's own name, or a silent choice between two tables

The paper lists the full set in its answer-guards table.

docs.title: Fact handles and detail
docs.text: Each answer returns an opaque, server-held handle per fact. The handle is bound to the dataset and the account. The rows behind a figure, a chart series and a written result table are derived by the server from the compiler's own query. Only the projection, one removed condition and a grouping change. No SQL comes from the browser.

docs.title: Progress trace
docs.text: The server records each stage of a request when it starts: route, understand, plan, query, read, decide. The reply returns the trace. The client can poll it while the request runs. Recording adds no model call and no query. A restricted principal's trace names no source beyond what the reply itself says.

docs.title: Entity 360
docs.text:
Entity 360 builds a report on one entity on request. It is read-only and finance only.

Section Source Profile, holdings Guarded SQL Evidence Visible links that carry the entity's key Concepts Concepts whose evidence passages belong to the entity Comparisons A stated value beside the recorded value, compared by code Summary Model text; code drops any sentence without a valid citation or with a number or name its cited items do not hold

The summary check is lexical, so the summary is labelled for review. Entities keep the key they are known by and are never merged. A name in a document never resolves to a customer identifier. The report is not evaluated against a gold set.

docs.title: Measured quality
docs.text: No unseen exam met the pass bar. Scores were 11, 14, 18 and 17 of 30. See Evaluation.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The task is a mapping. Given a semantic layer, decide for each unstructured passage which definitions it states a value of or is about. Or abstain. Then group that evidence into business concepts linked to the layer. The layer is never edited.

docs.title: The semantic layer
docs.text:
A semantic layer describes the tables of a warehouse. It names each field and metric and defines it. It declares how tables join.

In this system the layer is an Ossie YAML file per dataset. It holds tables, fields with descriptions and datatypes, declared relationships and metrics. The layer is given, not learned. The system reads it and never changes it.

Dataset Definitions in the layer Financial Services 143 Manufacturing 240

Each definition has a text card, a unit and a table. Declared relationships are many-to-one links between columns.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
The paper lists six inputs. The system learns or changes none of them.

Input What it is Structured data Tables with rows. CSV projections loaded read-only into private PostgreSQL. Semantic model Tables, fields, relationships and metrics in an Ossie file. Unstructured sources Documents, fill-in forms and audio. Files are pinned by SHA-256. Each carries a data label. Access policy Principals with roles and datasets, and the sources withheld from each restricted principal. Human decisions Corrections, approvals and rejections, the confirm of a build or a write, the publish of a release. Question A natural-language question and the asking principal.

Each source carries a data label: synthetic, public, or a cleaned sample file. Public files have scope extraction_only. They are linked to definitions. They are never induced into concepts and never tied to an entity.

docs.title: Passages
docs.text: A passage is a chunk of a readable source. It has text and context. The context is the title, the nearest heading and, for a call, the speaker. See Ingestion for how each file type is split.

docs.title: Evidence links
docs.text:
An evidence link records what a passage says in the terms of the layer. It holds the chunk, the definition, the relation, the stated value, the unit and the period. It also holds the entity keys of the chunk.

A passage can have up to three links, or none. None is a recorded outcome, not a gap.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
Relation Meaning states_value_of The passage states a value of this definition for an identifiable entity. is_about The passage discusses the definition but does not state its value. none No definition fits. The passage abstains.

The relation rule is strict. states_value_of needs a value of that definition for an identifiable entity. A promise, a target, an allegation, or a different unit, grain or period is is_about at most.

docs.title: Canonical definition
docs.text: Two fields joined by a declared relationship can hold one key. The canonical map follows a foreign-key column to the primary key it references. Each link stores both the selected definition and its canonical definition.

docs.title: Entity keys
docs.text:
Entity keys belong to the chunk, not to the selected definition. A key is found in one of three ways.

  • Stated. The chunk holds an existing value of a key column.
  • Derived. A stated key reaches another table through a declared relationship.
  • Inherited. The source states exactly one key of a table, and this chunk states none.

A mixed alphanumeric identifier resolves anywhere. A bare number resolves only next to a label derived from the model. A name alone resolves nothing.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
A concept is a business idea found in the evidence. Each concept is linked to definitions of the layer by a mapping predicate.

Origin Meaning both Anchored on a structured concept of the layer document Found in documents only

The predicates come from SKOS: exactMatch, closeMatch and relatedMatch. Code computes the predicate from evidence counts. A model does not choose it. See Pipeline B.

docs.title: The layer is never edited
docs.text:
The system does not change the semantic model. It does not merge entities or customers. It writes nothing to a shared table without a human confirm after a visible preview.

A concept points at definitions. It does not add fields to the layer. A release carries the base model plus the catalog in an extension block. The base model inside the release is unchanged.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Output What it holds A. Evidence links For each passage, the definitions it states a value of or is about, or none B. Concept catalog Business concepts found in the evidence, linked to definitions The answer One reply per question, every number computed by SQL or code

The paper defines outputs A and B. The workspace also writes table rows as a system feature. See Table rows.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Abstention A passage with no fitting definition keeps no link. The outcome is stored. Anchored concept A concept of the layer that collects its evidence by aggregation over links, with no model call. Candidate A concept or concept link below minimum support. It is stored and shown, not exported. Canonical definition The primary-key definition a foreign-key definition resolves to through declared relationships. Definition card The text of one definition used for retrieval: label, synonyms, description. Degraded A chunk whose model reply held no valid item. Evidence link A record (chunk, definition, relation, value, unit, period) with entity keys. False-link rate The share of passages with no fitting definition that still received a link. Guard A deterministic rule applied after the model decision. Release A versioned Ossie export of the approved catalog and the mapping corrections. Residual Passages whose links state no value. Only these reach the induction model. Retrieval proximity The combined keyword and embedding score of a definition for a passage. It is not a confidence. Restricted reader An account from which some sources are withheld. Withheld source A source a principal may not read. It is never read, cited or summarised for that principal.

The workspace ships two sample datasets: Financial Services and Manufacturing. All shipped data is synthetic or carries a public licence. Synthetic files say so inside the file. Public files keep their attribution and scope extraction_only.

Data leaves the process

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The workspace ships as an AMP for Cloudera AI. The AMP creates two jobs and one application. The jobs build a Python environment and the demo state. The application serves the workspace.

Untested on a real workspace

The AMP has not yet run on a real Cloudera AI workspace. The dependency lock records a tested macOS arm64 environment. Linux installation is untested. The public-host setting for the application proxy is an assumption until it runs.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
This page reports the paper's results with their scope. Evidence links reach useful precision with a low false-link rate on unseen synthetic packs. The catalog is below a usable level on recall. The question-answering path does not meet its pass bar on any unseen exam.

Read the scope of every number

The evaluation sets are small. One AI annotator wrote each set. There is no second annotator and no agreement statistic. Differences of a few points are not meaningful. No confidence intervals are reported. The sets cover two demo datasets. The paper does not claim state-of-the-art results.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Each gold row has a passage, a set of acceptable definitions (empty when none fits), a relation, and optionally a value and an entity. The selected definition is the first link, or none.

Metric Definition Precision Right selections over all selections Recall Right selections over rows with an acceptable definition False-link rate Rows with no acceptable definition that still got a link, over all such rows Offered@k Rows whose right definition is in the candidate list of size k, over positive rows Value and entity accuracy Exact-match rates on rows that carry them

Canonical variants compare canonical definitions on both sides.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
• An annotator who does not read the pipeline code writes each gold set.
  • Implementers never open held-out labels.
  • Settings are frozen before a held-out run.
  • The controller runs each held-out set once.
  • A set that has been read is relabelled development data.

docs.title: Pipeline A, held-out
docs.text:
Gold set A2: 82 anchors, 53 positive. Run once.

Method Precision Recall False-link rate Relation acc. Value acc. Entity acc. Threshold and rules 0.29 0.19 0.31 0.00 — — Interpreter, mistral-small 0.70 0.53 0.10 0.67 0.41 0.45 Interpreter, mistral-medium 0.58 0.26 0.07 0.52 0.34 0.40

Per dataset, small model: finance precision 1.00 (18 selected), recall 0.67; manufacturing precision 0.45 (22 selected), recall 0.38.

Later changes added guard G6, the canonical map, multi-link output and chunk-level entity keys. On the same set, canonical precision is then 0.82 and value accuracy 0.63. The set was development data by then, so these numbers are optimistic.

docs.title: Selection without a model
docs.text:
Held-out, run once (82 anchors, first gold set). Selection by score threshold and fitted compatibility rules.

Arm Precision Offered@12 Keyword only 0.40 0.49 Hybrid 0.27 0.73 Hybrid with passage context 0.21 0.76

The same rules reached 0.95 precision on the implementer's own examples. This gap motivated the model decision step and the held-out protocol.

docs.title: Pipeline A, unseen packs (test E24)
docs.text:
Each method run once with frozen settings. The two packs are generator-made planted truth. Only A3 is independently annotated. Precision / recall / false-link rate.

Method Finance pack (163 sentences, 104 positive) Manufacturing pack (212 sentences, 144 positive) Set A3 (52 rows, 13 positive) Hybrid-12 0.72 / 0.60 / 0.08 0.76 / 0.56 / 0.07 0.21 / 0.31 / 0.28 Hybrid-30 0.63 / 0.53 / 0.10 0.84 / 0.59 / 0.06 0.24 / 0.31 / 0.26 Expanded query 0.74 / 0.62 / 0.07 0.74 / 0.56 / 0.12 0.21 / 0.23 / 0.21 Two-step (default) 0.73 / 0.59 / 0.03 0.90 / 0.62 / 0.01 0.31 / 0.31 / 0.18
  • Two-step has the lowest false-link rate on all three sets.
  • Its cost is 1.7 calls per chunk, against 1.0 for hybrid-12.
  • Commitments are the weakest category. Every method links 0.00 to 0.12 of the finance commitments and 0.34 to 0.48 of the manufacturing commitments.
  • On A3, whose passages come mostly from product manuals, every method is poor. With 13 positive rows these numbers are rough.

docs.text:
The shortlist step drops the right definition. It reaches the decision call for 0.55 to 0.61 of commitment passages. The wide first-step list holds it for 0.94 to 0.95. This is the implementer's measurement.

Two switches aimed at this gap were tried and rejected. Synthetic packs, second use (development data).

Setting Finance pack Manufacturing pack Default (interp-v3, shortlist only) 0.73 / 0.59 / 0.03 0.90 / 0.62 / 0.015 interp-v4 0.62 / 0.57 / 0.10 0.83 / 0.63 / 0.04 Shortlist + 5 candidates 0.62 / 0.53 / 0.10 0.82 / 0.60 / 0.07

The commitment gap stays open.

docs.title: Pipeline B, concept gold set
docs.text:
39 concepts. Manufacturing has 21 gold concepts and 17 gold links. The first row is held-out. Later rows are development data.

Design Mfg. predicted Mfg. correct Mfg. precision Mfg. recall (of 17) Fin. correct (of 7) Free induction, model merge, model link 4 1 0.25 0.06 0 The same with two levels and linked entities 15 8 0.53 0.47 2 Anchored on Output A, narrow corpus, hybrid-12 10 7 0.70 0.41 0, not measurable Anchored, wider corpus, two-step 9 5 0.56 0.29 not scored The same with later rule changes 11 5 0.45 0.29 not scored

The score did not improve on the wider corpus. The corpus and the candidate method changed at once, so the cause is not isolated. One cause is visible: two-step abstains on contract headers and promise clauses. Pipeline B can only anchor what Pipeline A links.

Agreement between two resampled induction runs: manufacturing 0.83 (free, coarse) and 1.00 (residual only); finance 0.36 to 0.42. The finance corpus is too small and form-dominated for this number to carry weight.

docs.title: Table rows
docs.text: The table-write feature has no measured accuracy result. See Table rows.

docs.title: Question answering, unseen exams
docs.text:
Four exams, each with 30 questions, 15 per dataset: 4 database only, 4 documents only, 4 both, 3 with no supported answer. Each was written by an AI author who did not implement the answer path, and run once. The pass bar is 14 of 15 per dataset with every no-supported-answer question refused.

Exam 1 Exam 2 Exam 3 Exam 4 Finance (of 15) 3 7 9 9 Manufacturing (of 15) 8 7 9 8 Total (of 30) 11 14 18 17 Design first redesign round 3 round 4

No exam meets the pass bar. All four exams are spent. A fifth independent exam is needed for the next honest measure.

After rounds 5 and 6 of fixes, a replay of exam 4 gives 23 of 30. All four exams were development data by then. This is not evidence of unseen performance.

docs.title: Where the gap comes from
docs.text:
• Wrong measure, table or record. On exam 4, seven answers had facts or a conclusion the key rejects.
  • Right answers in another key shape. On replay, exam 4 has 23 strict passes and 27 right regardless of shape. The strict number is the reported one.
  • Capabilities not built. One plan holds one measure. Grouping, date arithmetic and relative phrases such as "last month" are not supported.

On the development set dev_wide (166 questions), mistral-small-latest answered 109 to 110 and mistral-medium-latest 115. About one in five reworded questions changed outcome on the small model (11 to 12 of 54).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Small sets, one annotator each: 82 anchors, 39 concepts, four exams of 30 questions, 166 development questions.
  • Only the first row of each results table for gold set A2 and the concept set is held-out.
  • Two demo datasets. The manufacturing documents total about 7 KB. The unseen packs are generated from data rows, so their wording is more regular than real documents.
  • The constants (k, the score clips, the 0.90 similarity, the support minima and the vote threshold) were chosen once and are untuned.
  • Several timings and inspections are implementer claims.

docs.title: Ingestion
docs.text:
Ingestion turns each source into passages. Each source is a file pinned by its SHA-256 hash. Each passage keeps its source, its revision and its span. The ingest route is /api/ocr. It has three readers: ocr, xfa-fields and text.

flowchart LR
  PDF[Printed PDF] -->|Mistral OCR| PG[Pages of markdown]
  XFA[Fill-in XFA form] -->|local read, no model| FL[Field listing]
  AUD[Recorded call] -->|Mistral transcription| SEG[Segments with speaker and time]
  TXT[Text document] -->|local read| PG
  PG --> U[Units: text, table, field]
  FL --> U
  SEG --> TU[Transcript units]
  U --> CH[Chunks]
  TU --> CH
  CH --> EMB[mistral-embed vectors]
  CH --> IDX[(LanceDB chunk index)]
  EMB --> IDX

docs.title: Printed PDF
docs.text:
The OCR reader sends the file to Mistral OCR. The default model is mistral-ocr-latest. MISTRAL_OCR_MODEL overrides it. A document may be at most 12 MiB.

OCR returns page markdown. It returns the tables of a page apart from the page text.

docs.title: Field passages
docs.text:
Printed label-and-value reports needed one change. The splitter read only the page text. One report therefore became a single chunk with no link.

Field passages put the tables back. Each labelled field becomes one passage, written as Label: value. Its section heading becomes its context. A heading-only passage is recorded without a model call.

The decision uses layout only, never a name or a title.

  • A two-column table qualifies when every label cell is bold.
  • A text block qualifies when at least three lines hold a short label, three or more spaces, and a value in one shared column.
  • A short line between blank lines in such a block becomes a heading.

Field passages are on by default. V2_FIELD_PASSAGES=0 turns them off. Every other source keeps identical chunks.

On one printed report, field passages changed 1 chunk with no link into 20 chunks with 13 links. That figure is the implementer's reading. No gold set scores it.

docs.title: Fill-in form
docs.text:
A fill-in XFA form holds its populated data in an embedded data packet. The xfa-fields reader reads that packet locally. No model sees the form at this step. It rejects a document type definition in the packet.

Each populated field becomes one line:

xfa:data/<group>[1]/<field>[1] = "<value>"

The field path keeps the field name and its position. A value with line breaks still takes one line.

docs.title: Template rows
docs.text:
For a document type with a declared template, field names drive table rows. A form field whose name equals a declared column yields a link with relation states_value_of. The link is recorded as a template link, method template:<type>, not as a model interpretation. These links feed table rows.

Template links share the evidence-link store with model links. Sources matched by a template are not sent to concept induction.

docs.title: Recorded call
docs.text:
The transcription reader sends the audio to Mistral. The default model is voxtral-mini-latest. MISTRAL_AUDIO_MODEL overrides it. The request asks for speaker separation and segment timestamps. A media file may be at most 25 MiB. A transcript may hold at most 1500 segments.

Each segment becomes one unit with:

  • the text,
  • the speaker label,
  • the start and end time in seconds,
  • the language.

Chunks keep the speaker and the time. A citation of a call therefore points to a speaker and a time range. Transcription takes no other options and no other reader.

docs.title: Text document
docs.text: Markdown and plain-text documents are read as text. They follow the same splitter as OCR page text.

docs.title: From units to chunks
docs.text:
Units are text, table, field or transcript units. Text units run through the inherited splitter. A table is never split. A field unit is one chunk.

Each chunk records:

Field Meaning order Position in the source page First page of the chunk start and end seconds Time range, for calls speaker Speakers of the chunk, for calls element kind text, table, field or transcript references Spans in the source text

The chunk context is the title, the nearest heading and, for calls, the speaker. Pipeline A queries with the passage text joined to this context.

docs.title: Embedding
docs.text:
Chunks are embedded with mistral-embed, 1024 dimensions, in batches of 16. The vector column may be empty, because an embedding call can fail. An embedding-space manifest pins the model, the dimension and the purpose. One index never mixes vector spaces.

Definition cards are embedded in the same space. An embedding cache keys each vector by space and text hash. On a new state, the card embeddings took 37 s and 110 s in two measured runs. These timings are the implementer's.

docs.title: Limits per source
docs.text: Setting Default Variable Chunks interpreted per source 256 V2_MAX_LINKED_CHUNKS Parallel decision calls 4 workers V2_INTERPRET_WORKERS Field passages on V2_FIELD_PASSAGES

docs.title: What leaves the process
docs.text:
Mistral receives the content of every processed file. The XFA reader is the exception for the read itself. It runs locally. Template links need no model call.

Public files

Public files keep scope extraction_only. They are linked to definitions. They are never induced into concepts and never attached to an entity.

docs.title: Localization
docs.text: The workspace UI shows English or Simplified Chinese. English is the default. A switch in the top bar stores the choice and reloads the page. The server keeps its English text. The browser translates what it shows.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  LS[(localStorage<br/>v2.lang)] --> I[i18n.js<br/>loads first]
  I --> D1[zh-CN.server.js]
  I --> D2[zh-CN.shell.js]
  I --> D3[zh-CN.pipeline.js]
  D1 --> P[Page scripts<br/>t and V2I18n.server]
  D2 --> P
  D3 --> P
  S[Server replies<br/>English codes and sentences] --> P

i18n.js loads before any page script. It reads the choice from localStorage['v2.lang']. The values are en and zh-CN. It sets the lang attribute of the document. The dictionary files register after it, one area per file.

If storage is blocked, the page uses English, and a new choice lasts for that page only.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Call Returns t(key, vars) The fixed text in the current language. A missing entry returns the English key. V2I18n.server(text) Text the server sent (a code, a label or a sentence), in Chinese or as sent V2I18n.number(n, options) Intl.NumberFormat for the current language; en-GB for English V2I18n.setLang(code) Stores the choice and reloads the page V2I18n.register(lang, entries) Adds dictionary entries

React pages import t and serverText from app/src/lib.js. They call them at render time, not at module load.

docs.title: Key convention
docs.text:
The English source text is the key: t('Confirm write'). Call sites stay readable. English needs no dictionary.

  • A sentence with values is one key with named placeholders: t('{count} rows in {table}', {count, table}).
  • Never build a sentence from translated fragments. Word order differs in Chinese.
  • Long sentences are keys too, word for word as English shows them.
  • Avoid plurals. When English needs them, choose the key by count.

docs.title: Server text
docs.text:
The server sends English codes and sentences. V2I18n.server looks each one up.

  1. An exact key match returns its Chinese entry.
  2. A key with {name} placeholders is also a pattern. It matches a sentence with any text in each placeholder.
  3. Chinese is used only when a key matches. Otherwise the text is shown as sent.

So a new server sentence never breaks the page. It shows in English until a dictionary entry exists.

docs.title: What is never translated
docs.text:
• Identifiers, ids, file names, table and column names, SQL, numbers, dates, units and masked values.
  • Product names: Cloudera, Cloudera AI, Iceberg, Trino, Spark, PostgreSQL, Semantic Hub.
  • data-* attribute values, CSS class names, aria-* ids, route hashes, option values.
  • Anything code compares: a reason code, a status, a step key.

Code compares the English value and translates only where the text is shown. For example, a refusal reason stays no supported answer in code.

docs.title: Markup safety
docs.text: Only text nodes are translated. Markup never passes through a dictionary entry. Inline markup inside a sentence uses a placeholder, built in code. Every user or data value is escaped before it reaches a placeholder. Attribute text is translated the same way and then escaped.

docs.title: Dictionary files
docs.text:
File Area i18n/zh-CN.server.js Server codes and sentences; holds the glossary i18n/zh-CN.shell.js The workspace shell i18n/zh-CN.pipeline.js The React pages

Each file holds one call: window.V2I18n?.register('zh-CN', { ... }). The object is strict JSON. One area per file means parallel work never edits one shared file.

A new dictionary file must be added in two places:

  • index.html, after i18n.js;
  • ASSETS in semantic_pipeline_v2/workspace_server.py.

A server started before a file joined ASSETS returns 404 for it. That page keeps English. workspace.js defines an English fallback when i18n.js is missing.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
The glossary heads zh-CN.server.js. Every file uses its terms.

English Chinese evidence link 证据链接 concept catalog 概念目录 semantic layer 语义层 release 发布版本 passage 段落 restricted reader 受限读者

docs.title: Masking and Chinese text
docs.text: Identifier masking uses ASCII character classes. An identifier written next to Chinese text with no space still stands as a token and is masked. See Access and masking.

docs.title: Table rows
docs.text:
The workspace can write table rows from documents, forms and recorded calls. This is a system feature. The paper defines two outputs, A (evidence links) and B (the concept catalog), and does not cover it. The feature has no measured accuracy result.

Every write needs a preview and an explicit confirm. Rows are insert-only, so a replay adds nothing.

docs.title: Four source shapes
docs.text: Source What it does Target Fill-in form A form field whose name equals a declared column yields a cell A declared table Printed report A printed label maps to a declared column through a label map; a label with no mapping is left out The same declared tables Recorded call One row per approved stated value, keyed by the customer identifier the call states A long table, ext_call_fact Document with no declared table A table proposed from the document's own labels A new table, ext_<name>

docs.title: Fill-in forms
docs.text:
A form field is matched to a declared column by its exact name. The match yields a link with relation states_value_of and method template:<type>. It is recorded as a template link, not as a model interpretation. An empty field states nothing and yields no cell.

The demo finance model declares two tables.

Table Notes STR_Transaction The transaction group of a form STR_AccountEntity Account columns; no identity number, name or contact column

The two tables join on the source revision.

docs.title: Printed reports
docs.text: A printed report states label-and-value pairs, such as "Account number: ...". A label map in code names, for each declared column, the label that states it and how to read the value. A label with no entry in the map is left out. The map in the code covers one report layout. Another layout needs its own map.

docs.title: Recorded calls
docs.text: The long table has one row per approved stated value. Its columns are customer_id, field, definition, value, unit, period, passage, source_file and chunk_id. Only links a person approved or corrected count. The call must state exactly one customer identifier among its approved links, or the preview is refused.

docs.title: A table proposed from a document
docs.text:
When no declared table fits a document, the workspace can propose a table from the labels the document prints. The document needs at least three labelled fields.

  • Each label becomes a column.
  • Code infers the column type: date, money, integer, decimal, otherwise text.
  • A value that looks like a number but has a leading zero stays text.
  • A field whose label names an identifier (number, no, id, reference, code) stays text.
  • The table name is ext_doc_ plus the document title and a short fingerprint of its column names.
  • The same labels give the same table, so a later file appends to it.
  • A file with other labels is refused by name, and no column is added to an existing table.

docs.title: Several sources in one write
docs.text: One preview can name up to 20 sources. The server suggests other readable sources whose evidence links or labels fill the same tables. Code decides the group by comparing the tables each source fills. A model then writes one sentence, the hint, on why the suggested files fit. The model sees file, table and field names only. A failed or odd reply drops the sentence and keeps the suggestion. The hint is labelled as AI-written.

docs.title: Answer results
docs.text: An answer result can also be written as a table. It goes to an insert-only table in schema v2_ask of the private PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Preview and confirm
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as Administrator
  participant S as Server
  participant PG as Private PostgreSQL
  participant T as Trino / Iceberg
  U->>S: preview (form, document, call or answer)
  S->>S: build rows, type-check each cell
  S-->>U: rows, fingerprint, one-use approval, generated Spark job
  U->>S: confirm (fingerprint, approval)
  S->>PG: insert missing rows
  alt Trino route configured
    S->>T: CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, insert missing rows, count
    T-->>S: rows read back
  end
  S-->>U: labels, snapshot read from the written table
  • The preview is read-only.
  • When the Trino route is configured, the preview also asks the lakehouse to validate the insert, without running it. A table the lakehouse will refuse shows as a warning before any confirm. A table that does not exist yet is not a refusal. A check that cannot run says nothing; the confirm still reports its own result.
  • Each cell is type-checked. A value that fails the column's type or unit check is rejected and not written.
  • A confirm needs the preview's fingerprint and its one-use approval.
  • The approval expires after 10 minutes.
  • Writes are limited to the administrator.
  • A correction made after a preview makes it stale. The confirm then refuses until a new preview.

Each stored cell keeps its source, revision, chunk id and quoted span in v2_physical_rows. The stored cell holds the masked value of an identity number.

After a confirm, the reply holds a snapshot read from the written table itself. It shows the row count, the number of new rows and the first rows.

docs.title: The two write paths to Iceberg
docs.text:
The local private PostgreSQL write is the default. It always runs first. Two routes reach Iceberg. The Spark script is always generated and is always available for download.

Direct, through TrinoGenerated Spark job

The server writes the same tables, columns and rows through Cloudera Lakehouse Engine (Trino). It runs under the platform user's own rights.

For each table it runs three statements:

  1. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.
  2. INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS on one combined key per row.
  3. A count of the rows now present, read back through Trino.

Each statement is safe to repeat, so a dropped connection is retried. Every table and column name must be a plain identifier. Every value is a quoted literal.

The route is on only when all of these hold:

Variable Meaning V2_ICEBERG_ROUTE Must be trino V2_TRINO_URL Base URL of the Trino endpoint CDE_TOKEN A bearer token; the Trino user is the token's subject V2_TRINO_CA Optional CA file for TLS verification

With this route the Spark job is generated for download only.

Every preview also generates the Cloudera Data Engineering Spark job that would write the same rows to Iceberg. The job holds a PySpark script, a job specification and a submit command line with credential placeholders.

The job creates the tables if missing. It runs an insert-only MERGE keyed on source id, revision and row key. It then checks the row count. The catalog credential is referenced as a workload secret in the job specification. No credential appears in the specification, the script or the response.

The reply labels the job "Spark job generated, not submitted" unless it is really submitted. No job id, status or count is invented.

docs.title: Which route runs
docs.text:
Configuration What a confirm does Trino route set Local write, then Trino write; Spark job offered for download Iceberg connection set, preview named Iceberg, no Trino route Local write, then the Spark job is submitted Neither Local write; Spark job generated, not submitted

A failure after the local write is reported. The local write is never rolled back.

docs.title: The insert-only rule
docs.text:
A replay must add nothing. The local table has a unique key on dataset, source revision, table and row key. The Trino insert compares one combined key per row.

The combined key exists for a reason. An earlier condition used several null-safe comparisons over a multi-row value list. The engine returned too few matches, and a replay inserted one duplicate row. The condition now compares one combined key.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• There is no schema editor. A proposed table keeps the name and columns the code gives it.
  • A table that exists with other columns is refused. Columns are never added to it.
  • The workspace reads only the layouts described above. Other layouts give no rows.
  • The label map covers one printed report layout.
  • No accuracy is measured for these routes.

docs.title: Pipeline A: evidence links
docs.text:
Pipeline A turns one passage into evidence links, or into an abstention. A model picks among retrieved definitions. Code then checks the value, settles the relation, resolves the canonical definition and attaches entity keys.

Input: chunks of readable sources, the semantic model, the structured data (for entity keys). Output: Output A, one or more evidence-link records per chunk.

Figure 2 of the paper. Blue steps call a language model. White steps are code. A passage with an empty shortlist or no fitting definition keeps no link.

docs.title: The five steps
docs.text: Step Who What 1 Score Code Keyword and embedding scores for every definition, combined 2 Shortlist Model Picks at most five definitions from the top list 3 Decide Model Returns at most three links: definition, relation, value, unit, period 4 Guard Code Guards G1 to G6 check value, unit, allegation and key 5 Resolve Code Canonical definition and entity keys

docs.title: 1. Score
docs.text:
The query is the passage with its context. Each definition has a text card.

Two scores are computed for every definition.

  • Embedding. The cosine between the passage and the card, both from mistral-embed. It is turned into a standard score over the whole catalog. The standard score removes the per-query offset of embedding similarity.
  • Keyword. A keyword score over labels, synonyms and descriptions.

Both are clipped to the range 0 to 1. The keyword score is divided by 45. The standard score maps 2.0 to 0 and 4.5 to 1. The two are combined so that strong evidence from either leg counts:

r = 1 - (1 - keyword) * (1 - embedding)

The constants 45, 2.0 and 4.5 were set on development data and are not tuned further.

Retrieval proximity is not confidence

r is retrieval proximity. It is not a confidence.

docs.title: 2. Shortlist
docs.text:
The default candidate method is two-step.

Setting Value Variable Catalog size at or below which the whole catalog is offered 150 V2_WHOLE_CATALOG_MAX First-step list size otherwise, by retrieval score 60 V2_SHORTLIST_POOL Shortlist size at most 5 — Extra retrieval candidates added to a shortlist 0 V2_SHORTLIST_EXTRA Prompts shortlist-v2, then interp-v3 V2_INTERPRET_PROMPT for the second

A model reads a compact list: id, label and one line per definition. It returns at most five ids. A reply naming an id outside the list is invalid. Nothing is substituted. An empty shortlist is an abstention, with no second call.

The first design used hybrid-12: the union of the top 12 of each leg. Embedding ranking alone placed the right definition in the top 12 for only 0.52 (finance) and 0.69 (manufacturing) of positive passages on development data. A short single list therefore caps recall. That result motivated a wide first list with a model shortlist.

V2_CANDIDATE_VARIANT selects another method: lexical, vector, hybrid12, hybrid30, hybrid50, expanded or two_step.

docs.title: 3. Decide
docs.text:
The decision model is mistral-small-latest, at temperature 0, with prompt interp-v3. V2_INTERPRETER_MODEL overrides the model. It reads the passage, its context and the full cards of the shortlist. It returns at most three links, or none. Each link names a distinct definition from the shortlist.

An invalid item is dropped and noted. If every item is invalid, the chunk is stored as degraded. Per-chunk calls run on a shared pool of four workers by default.

docs.title: 4. Guards
docs.text:
Guards run after the model.

Guard Condition Effect G1 value grounding The normalised value does not occur in the normalised passage The value is removed G2 allegation The passage matches an allegation pattern and the relation is states_value_of The relation becomes is_about G3 constrained field Allegation wording, and the definition is a constrained field The link is withdrawn G4 unit conflict states_value_of, the value has a unit family, and the definition's unit is not in it The relation becomes is_about G5 no value states_value_of with no value The relation becomes is_about G6 key value The canonical definition is a key column, and the passage holds exactly one existing value of it The value becomes that key; the relation becomes states_value_of

In the code, G3 also fires for a constrained field in any adverse-media source, with or without allegation wording. The guards enforce one rule. states_value_of needs a value of that definition for an identifiable entity. A promise, a target, an allegation, or a different unit, grain or period is is_about at most.

docs.title: Canonical definition
docs.text: Two fields joined by a declared relationship can hold one key. The canonical map follows a non-key foreign-key column to the primary key it references. Each link stores both the selected definition and the canonical one. Strict metrics compare the selected definition. Canonical metrics compare the canonical one on both sides.

docs.title: Entity keys
docs.text:
Entity keys belong to the chunk.

flowchart LR
  T[Chunk text and context] -->|labelling rule| ST[Stated keys]
  ST -->|declared relationship| DE[Derived keys]
  SRC[Other chunks of the same source] -->|exactly one key of a table| IN[Inherited keys]
  ST --> E[Entity keys of the chunk]
  DE --> E
  IN --> E
  • A mixed alphanumeric identifier resolves anywhere.
  • A bare number resolves only next to a label derived from the model: a column name or the entity word of the table.
  • A name alone resolves nothing.

Each key is tagged with how it was found: stated, derived or inherited.

docs.title: The stored record
docs.text:
Each link holds:

  • chunk, source, source revision and span;
  • definition and canonical definition;
  • relation, stated value, unit, period;
  • entity keys;
  • candidates and scores (at most 50 stored);
  • method and model revision;
  • status: proposed, degraded, corrected, rejected or not_processed;
  • actor and time.

Links are stored in table v2_evidence_links. They can be exported as JSON lines from /api/evidence-links/export.

docs.title: What the model does and what code does
docs.text: Model Code Picks at most five candidate ids Scores every definition Picks up to three definitions and a relation Validates every id against the offered list Copies a value, unit and period Checks the value occurs in the passage Downgrades or withdraws relations by rule Resolves canonical definitions and entity keys

docs.title: Results in brief
docs.text: On the held-out gold set A2 (82 anchors, run once), the model decision step reached precision 0.70. Thresholds and rules reached 0.29. On unseen synthetic packs, two-step reached a false-link rate of 0.03 (finance) and 0.01 (manufacturing). Commitments are the weakest category. See Evaluation.

docs.title: Pipeline B: concept catalog
docs.text:
Pipeline B reads all evidence links and writes a versioned concept catalog. Concepts of the layer collect their evidence by aggregation, with no model call. Code computes each mapping predicate from evidence counts. Only passages the layer cannot explain reach an induction model.

Input: Output A after human corrections, the chunks, the semantic model. Output: Output B, a versioned concept catalog and its Ossie export.

The input links exclude rejected, degraded and unprocessed records.

flowchart LR
  L[Links after corrections] --> SP{6 Split}
  SP -->|all links| AN[7 Anchor<br/>aggregate per layer concept]
  AN --> PR[8 Predicate<br/>from counts and names]
  SP -->|residual| IND[9 Induce<br/>model]
  IND --> MG[10 Merge<br/>model confirms complete groups]
  MG --> VT[11 Vote<br/>2 of 4 runs]
  PR --> OB[(Output B)]
  VT --> OB

Steps 9 and 10 call a model. Steps 6, 7, 8 and 11 are code.

docs.title: 6. Split
docs.text:
The residual is the set of chunks whose links all have relation is_about or none. In other words, the residual holds passages with no stated value.

Three kinds of chunk never enter the residual:

  • chunks of sources matched by a form template (table rows);
  • chunks of public sources;
  • chunks with a stated value.

A clause chunk that also states an identifier is induced.

docs.title: 7. Anchor
docs.text:
Each structured concept of the layer is bound to a set of definitions. Its evidence is every chunk with a link whose canonical definition is in that set. No model is called.

For a concept and a definition, each supporting chunk counts once. It counts as states_value_of when one of its links states a value that fits the definition. Otherwise it counts as is_about.

docs.title: 8. Predicate
docs.text:
The mapping predicate is derived, not asked of a model.

Predicate Condition exactMatch More states_value_of than is_about chunks; more than half of the value chunks select a definition of the same structured concept; and a shared normalised name closeMatch More states_value_of than is_about chunks, otherwise relatedMatch Otherwise

Stated values show that passages talk about the field. Only a shared name shows that the concept means what the field records.

The name test compares the concept's label and synonyms with the label, technical name and synonyms of the definition.

docs.title: Link status
docs.text:
Status Condition proposed At least one value chunk, or at least two is_about chunks, or one is_about clause that states a value and a unit or a period candidate Otherwise

The predicate rule changed so that closeMatch can fire. Its agreement with the gold predicates has not been measured since that change.

docs.title: 9. Induce
docs.text: An induction model proposes concepts from the residual. The model is mistral-small-latest. One concept is one obligation, event, measure, party or attribute. It has one unit, one grain and one party role.

docs.title: 10. Merge
docs.text:
Each concept has a signature: type, unit, role and the canonical definitions it links to. Two concepts are compatible when no component conflicts.

Candidate pairs come from embedding similarity above 0.90 among compatible pairs. A model confirms each pair. The model is mistral-medium-latest.

A set is merged only if it is a complete group. Every pair in the group must be compatible and confirmed. This forbids chains: concept 1 matching concept 2 and concept 2 matching concept 3 does not merge 1 with 3.

docs.title: 11. Vote
docs.text:
Induction runs on the full residual set and on three resamples of 80% of it, with fixed seeds.

Status Condition proposed Found in at least 2 of the 4 runs candidate Otherwise

Candidates are stored and shown. They are not exported.

docs.title: The concept record
docs.text:
Field Meaning id, label, meaning, synonyms, examples What the concept is origin both (anchored on a structured concept) or document (found in documents only) type, unit, grain The signature parts links Definitions with a SKOS predicate and evidence counts evidence Passages that support the concept status proposed or candidate; reviewers may correct or reject level and parent Position in a two-level hierarchy

Concepts are versioned rows in v2_catalog_concept.

docs.title: Build and incremental update
docs.text:
A build is a preview followed by a confirm: /api/catalog/build/preview, then /api/catalog/build/confirm.

  • A failed model reply does not abort a build.
  • A unit is retried a bounded number of times.
  • A build fails only when more than 10% of units fail.
  • Adding one document reuses cached links and keeps every earlier concept id.

The implementer measured a rebuild with cached links at 67 s and 54 s. Adding one document took 8.6 s and 7.6 s with 6 model calls.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: The catalog is exported in the Ossie format. The structured concepts and the catalog concepts sit in one concept block. The export passes the Semantic Hub schema check and lint. See Review and release.

docs.title: Results in brief
docs.text:
On the concept gold set, the anchored design reached link precision 0.70 and recall 0.41 on the first (narrow) corpus. That row is development data. The held-out first row, free induction, reached 0.25 and 0.06. On the wider corpus with two-step, precision fell to 0.45 and recall stayed at 0.29.

Pipeline B can only anchor what Pipeline A links. Output A commitment recall therefore limits Output B. See Evaluation.

docs.title: Review and release
docs.text:
People decide what the system believes. A reviewer approves, corrects or rejects evidence links, concepts and concept links. An administrator publishes the approved catalog as a versioned release. Only approved concepts of the latest release reach answers.

flowchart LR
  A[(Output A links)] --> R{Reviewer}
  B[(Output B concepts)] --> R
  R -->|approve, correct, reject| C[(Correction rows<br/>appended, with actor)]
  C --> O[Overlay on read]
  O --> PV[Publish preview<br/>content SHA-256]
  PV -->|admin confirm, same fingerprint| REL[(Release vN<br/>Ossie export)]
  REL -->|approved concepts only| ASK[Answer path]

docs.title: Corrections
docs.text:
A correction is an appended row. It records the dataset, the kind, the key, the patch, the actor and the time. The pipeline records are never changed. Corrections are overlaid on read.

Kind What a patch may change Evidence link Relation, stated value, unit, period, definition, status Concept Label, definition, status Concept link SKOS predicate, status

Statuses are proposed, corrected and rejected. An approval is a patch that sets status corrected. A rejection sets status rejected.

Concept-link predicates may be exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch or relatedMatch. Code proposes exactMatch, closeMatch or relatedMatch. A reviewer may choose any of the five.

docs.title: Approve all
docs.text:
Approve all approves the listed links or concepts in one transaction. Each item passes the checks of a single correction. One unknown or withheld item refuses the whole request. Rejected and already approved items are skipped, so a second click writes nothing.

Approval is the only gate

An approved but doubtful link shapes answers. The paper gives one example: "sales tax" linked to a purchase-order tax field. Approval, including the one-click Approve all, is the only gate.

docs.title: Corrections survive a rebuild
docs.text: Corrections are keyed by the concept id, by the concept and definition, or by the chunk and its original definition. A rebuild keeps earlier concept ids. Corrections therefore overlay the rebuilt catalog the same way.

docs.title: Effect on other outputs
docs.text: Corrections reach Pipeline B, which reads links after corrections. They also reach table rows. A rejected template link shows as a cell removed by a reviewer. A corrected value is checked again and marked with its actor. A correction made after a row preview makes that preview stale.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
A release is the dataset's base model plus an extension block. The extension holds:

  • the catalog concepts, without candidates and without anything a correction rejected;
  • their definition links, without rejected links;
  • evidence references;
  • the saved mapping corrections;
  • a release block.

The base model inside the release is unchanged. Releases are rows of v2_release in the private PostgreSQL. Nothing else is written.

docs.title: Preview and confirm
docs.text:
Publishing is limited to the administrator.

  1. The preview computes the release and its fingerprint, the content SHA-256.
  2. The confirm recomputes the release and writes it only if the fingerprint still matches.

The history lists every version. A release with content from a source the account cannot read is hidden from that account.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: The release is an Ossie YAML file. The export passes the Semantic Hub schema check and lint. Each version can be downloaded from /api/publish/release.

docs.title: What reaches answers
docs.text:
Item Reaches answers Approved concept in the latest release Yes Proposed concept in the latest release No Candidate concept No; candidates are never exported Concept in an older release No Concept with any evidence passage withheld from the reader No, for that reader Evidence links Their entity keys are read by the answer path

A concept is left out for a reader when any one of its evidence passages is withheld from that reader. The concept's label and synonyms are written from all its passages. One withheld passage could leak through them.

The switch V2_ASK_CATALOG controls this input. It is on (published) by default. Any other value turns it off.

docs.title: How approved concepts are used
docs.text: When a question states the label or a synonym of an approved concept, the answer path offers that name. It offers the name beside the definitions the concept links with exactMatch, or else with closeMatch. Narrowing rules keep a name out in several cases. See Ask.

docs.title: Measured effect
docs.text:
The paper replayed every development set with the catalog off, on with no release, and on with every anchored concept approved. No question changed status or answer in any set. A concept named a usable definition in 23 of 296 questions. The plan used that definition in 16. The structured model already carries almost every useful synonym.

The mechanism broke no answer on these sets. A benefit is not shown. A benefit needs data whose business vocabulary differs from the model's names. These are the implementer's numbers on recorded replies.

docs.title: 语义工作区
docs.text:
语义工作区把非结构化来源映射到一个给定且从不编辑的语义层上。 来源包括文档、可填写表单和通话录音。 结果是证据链接和有锚点的概念目录。 工作区还可以把写出表行作为一项系统功能，论文没有涉及它。 问答工作区读取这些结果，并引用每个回答背后的段落。

本站介绍设计和细节。 内容来自工作论文和代码。 本站不含实验练习。

论文的图 1。 (a) 构建时，管线 A 把段落链接到给定的语义模型（输出 A）。 管线 B 把这些证据归并为概念（输出 B）。 由人批准并发布一个发布版本。 (b) 提问时，规则优先的路由器把每个请求送到四个固定工具之一；只有当规则无法补全一条操作请求时才由模型协助。

docs.title: 为什么需要它
docs.text:
结构化数据有语义层。 语义层为每个字段和指标命名并给出定义，还声明表如何连接。 合同、表单和通话录音没有这样的层。 它们包含的限额、日期和承诺，无法与表连接，也无法与表一起治理。

论文把这一缺口看作映射任务。 对每个段落，判断它陈述了哪些定义的值、或与哪些定义相关，或者弃权。 然后把这些证据归并为与语义层相连的业务概念。 语义层是目标。系统从不编辑它。

docs.title: 规则
docs.text:
整个设计遵循一条规则：模型选择，代码决定。

  • 小型语言模型在检索到的定义中做选择。
  • 确定性防护规则检查陈述的值、确定关系并附加实体键。
  • 语义层的概念通过聚合收集证据，不调用模型。
  • 只有语义层无法解释的段落才会进入归纳模型。
  • 提问时，代码计算每个数字。模型编写计划并读取条款中的值。

docs.title: 主要结果与限制
docs.text:
论文报告了以下结果。每个结果的适用范围是结论的一部分。

结果 数值 范围 链接精确率，模型决策步骤 0.70 留出的金标准集 A2，运行一次，82 个锚点 链接精确率，阈值和规则 0.29 同一数据集 未见数据包上的精确率，两步法 0.73（金融），0.90（制造） 生成器制作的合成数据包，运行一次 未见数据包上的误链接率，两步法 0.03（金融），0.01（制造） 同样的数据包 问答，未见考试 30 题中的 11、14、18 和 17 四场考试；没有一场达到通过线

论文声明的限制

对承诺的召回率是主要限制。 评估集很小，每个集由一位 AI 标注员编写。 这些集合覆盖两个演示数据集。 问答路径在任何未见考试上都未达到通过线。 论文不声称达到最先进水平。

每张表及其范围见评估。

docs.title: 阅读指南
docs.text:
按以下顺序阅读设计部分。

  1. 概念：任务、术语和词汇表。
  2. 架构：构建时、提问时、组件和数据存储。
  3. 摄取：每种文件类型如何变成段落。
  4. 管线 A：从段落到证据链接。
  5. 管线 B：从证据链接到概念目录。
  6. 审核与发布：人工决定，以及什么会进入回答。

使用和运维部分请阅读以下页面。

  • 提问：问答路径、路由器、拒答和引用。
  • 表行：来自表单、打印报告、通话和文档的表行，以及两条写入路径。
  • 访问与掩码：账户、不可见来源和标识符掩码。
  • 本地化：英文和中文的语言切换。
  • 部署：Cloudera AI 上的 AMP。
  • 数据：两个示例数据集及其许可。
